mcat_description.short: Log Homes are prefabricated or site-built residential and hospitality structures constructed from stacked solid timber logs or engineered wood, supplied as complete turnkey builds or modular kit systems. They are sold as finished structures quoted per square foot of built-up area.
mcat_description.long: Log Homes in the Indian market are prefabricated timber structures built from solid wood logs, glulam panels, or engineered timber, designed for residential, resort, and eco-tourism applications. Manufacturers typically supply end-to-end — design, factory fabrication, transport, and on-site assembly — with wall thicknesses commonly ranging from 90–120 mm for external log walls. Wood species used include pine (including glulam-finish pine), cedar, deodar, and imported FSC/PEFC-certified timber from British Columbia and Scandinavian sources. The category spans compact single-room cabins to multi-bedroom villas and resort cottage clusters, with roofing in galvanised steel, wood shingles, or thatch, and optional PUF insulation panels for hill-station thermal performance.

market_context: Log Homes in India are a growing segment within the broader prefabricated structures market, driven primarily by the expansion of eco-tourism, glamping, boutique resorts, and hill-station second-home demand. Multiple Indian manufacturers (Deodar Log Homes, Royal Prefab, YRS Prefab, Loom Crafts, Prefab Wooden Homes) operate in this space, offering end-to-end design-fabricate-install services. The dominant construction method is prefabricated modular assembly — sections are factory-built and assembled on-site, reducing build time to 45–90 days versus conventional construction timelines. External wall materials range from solid stacked logs to glulam-finish pine panels (commonly 90–100 mm thick) and engineered timber frames; roofing uses galvanised steel (29-gauge), wood shingles, or thatch. Timber sourcing includes both domestic species (deodar, pine) and imported FSC/PEFC-certified timber from British Columbia and Scandinavia. Key buyer segments are resort/hospitality developers, individual landowners building farmhouses or hill-station retreats, and eco-tourism operators. The category overlaps with Wooden Houses and Prefabricated Wooden Houses in buyer vocabulary — 'log cabin', 'wooden cabin', and 'timber cottage' are used interchangeably by buyers. No single dominant Indian brand controls the market; it is fragmented across regional manufacturers. BIS standards for timber construction (IS 883 for structural timber, IS 1038 for wood treatment) are relevant but not universally cited by sellers in this segment (single-source observation — low confidence for BIS adoption rate).
